reason: Changing mark_attended to a time window left a run-sheet claim, a seed-script comment and the demo plan saying the staff door was deliberately not time-gated. Nothing in the library tells a session to sweep prose claims after a gate change; the role-gate skill covers role gates only.

Check-in gate change left a copy-voice mismatch: a comment on `checkInClosedMessage` claimed one shared source, but the attendee confirm page and its server action kept their own literals. The sweep also found an open O7 row in the execution plan that the change closed but nobody had marked.

DB-02 review round: the migration moved check-in to event_occurrences rows, but no UPDATE path synced them to events.start_time/end_time. Both dev and backtest reviewers found it only after the fallback was deleted. The sweep skill should force the writer-side check.
Dev-lens review found a soft-delete gate that held for RLS reads while admin-client pages still rendered deleted events. The sweep rule did not cover readers that bypass RLS.

A stub-vs-real switch was landed; the readers keyed on the same env flag (EmailDeliveryStrip "stubbed" pill, RegisterCard "dev mode" copy, PassDeliveryPanel) and TEMP-marked stub branches were the claims that could go stale. This is the same class as a changed gate leaving old claims behind.
The trigger missed the stub-vs-real send switch, so the sweep bullet added alongside would not load when that switch flips. Widen the trigger to cover it.

Flipping the email send switch to error-on-missing-key changed three things the existing sweep did not name: the retry budget spends in minutes, production banners and strips still said 'development stub' or 'stalled', and the cron JSON still reported delivery 'stubbed' with ok false. The sweep bullet only greps the flag names, so it missed copy that never mentions the flag.

Sweep path list missed the root CLAUDE.md. Hard Rule 7 there still claimed sends are stubbed regardless of stage, which is false for a production build once the send switch flips. The sweep must cover root-level rule files.

The retry-budget trap was found only by execution. Writing a failed row per recipient per tick under a missing key exhausts MAX_SEND_ATTEMPTS in three ticks and strands rows as gaveUp. The rule should name the fix (batch error, no rows) so the next switch flip starts there.

The production-only signal reaches more environments than the name suggests. A key-less Preview would now error, but the deploy plan's env matrix says the key is production-only. The sweep should force that comparison before a flip.
